overview: A Pacific system brings rain and mountain snow to the Cascades through Thursday, then a stronger trough with a river of moisture pushes into the Northwest and Northern Rockies Friday into Saturday. Tahoe and the Northeast get weaker, shorter systems across the holiday.

regions.title: Cascades
regions.text: A stream of Pacific moisture keeps rain and snow falling on the Cascades through Thursday, with snow levels high and mostly rain below the peaks. Crystal Mountain has the best setup, with 37 inches expected through Sunday, most of it Thursday and Friday. Strong south winds will gust near 48 mph Thursday.

regions.title: Northern Rockies
regions.text: A trough moves in Friday, with southwest winds lifting snow over the western Wyoming and Montana ranges through Saturday. Grand Targhee has the strongest totals, 42 inches through Sunday, with its biggest day Saturday. Fog is likely in valleys Wednesday morning, and Thanksgiving stays dry and mild.

regions.title: Coast Mountains
regions.text: Wet, mild weather continues in the Coast Mountains, with rain on and off through the week and mountain snow mostly staying above the resorts. Whistler's biggest day is Wednesday, with 30 inches expected through Sunday. Expect showers rather than steady snow on most days.

regions.title: Northeast
regions.text: Cold, dry air holds through Thursday morning, then a storm brings rain to the Northeast late Thanksgiving into Friday, with a brief freezing rain or wintry mix at first at higher elevations. Killington and Stowe see 17 inches through Sunday, peaking Thursday or Friday. Strong easterly winds gust near 68 mph Thursday night at Killington.

regions.title: Kootenays
regions.text: Mild, rainy weather covers the Kootenays through Thursday, with snow levels rising to near 1000 metres at times. Whitewater sees the most snow, 16 inches through Sunday, with its big day Thursday. Colder air returns by Sunday night, bringing flurries.

regions.title: Tahoe
regions.text: Rain and breezy southeast winds move through Tahoe overnight, with mostly dry weather returning Wednesday afternoon and warmer temperatures through the holiday. A stronger storm arrives Sunday, bringing rain and snow to the Sierra. Sugar Bowl is the top pick, with 18 inches on Sunday.

regions.title: Central Rockies
regions.text: Mild, dry weather lasts through Thanksgiving, with patchy valley fog likely Wednesday morning. A system brings snow showers Friday through Sunday, with the highest confidence over the Park Range. Steamboat expects 16 inches through Sunday, most of it Saturday, though totals to the south depend on how deep the trough digs.

regions.title: Okanagan
regions.text: Showers arrive Wednesday night and continue Thursday as a weather system passes. After a drier Friday and Saturday, cooler air brings a chance of flurries Sunday night. Big White is the top pick, with 11 inches through Sunday, most of it Thursday.

ahead.text: The Climate Prediction Center expects above-normal precipitation across most of the Lower 48 for Nov 30 to Dec 4, with the highest chances over California and Nevada.

sources.name: NOAA buoys 51001 / 51101 (method: Powder Buoy, Mike Ruzek)

buoy.text: Buoys 51001 and 51101 near Hawaii popped Nov 11, the swell signal Powder Buoy watches for a Wasatch storm about two weeks later — here Nov 22–28. In past winters a pop raised the chance of a Wasatch storm in that window by roughly 6 to 12 points. Experimental: promising, not proven.
